# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

**On notes:** Always signal cooperation and sustainability early. "Fishing my share" anchors expectations and encourages matching behavior from other players. This establishes a cooperative equilibrium that benefits everyone, including me.

**On sustainable share calculations:** The sustainable share is your baseline for responsible fishing. Land at or very close to it consistently across all seasons—this keeps the stock healthy and signals to Coop that you're not a threat.

**On Coop's threat:** Take it seriously. If the fleet defects and lands above quota together, Coop will crash the ground. Monitor the landing pattern across seasons. If others start exceeding the sustainable share, assume Coop will retaliate and the stock will collapse.

**On the season quota:** You can land up to 9 within quota, but only do so when you're confident others won't escalate. Landing 9 when others are landing 8.3 is noticeable and risks breaking cooperation.

**On the final season:** The final season is tempting but not a reliable place to defect. In this game, cooperation held so completely that landing 9 in season 6 worked—but that was because everyone else maintained 8.3. Do not assume others will cooperate in the final round. Landing consistently at 8.3 across all six seasons would have yielded 49.8, nearly matching my actual score of 50.5. The marginal gain from the final-season push to 9 was minimal and risky.

**On consistency:** The strongest cooperative signal is unwavering consistency. Landing exactly 8.3 every single season (or as close as possible) creates no variation for others to interpret as defection or weakness. Every deviation from the pattern is a moment of ambiguity.

**On early seasons:** Resist the temptation to maximize each round. Your total score is what matters. A steady 8.3 per season across six seasons compounds to a strong total without the risk of cascading defection.

**On patience:** Cooperation can hold across an entire game if you commit to it fully. Do not treat the final season as license to break the pattern. Treat it as confirmation that the pattern was the right call all along.

**What to do differently next time:** Land 8.3 consistently in every season, including the final one. The security of maintaining perfect cooperation and demonstrating absolute reliability is worth more than the marginal gain from defecting at the end.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I see the fleet signaling cooperation through notes about fishing their share, I signal the same thing back. This establishes and maintains the cooperative equilibrium.

When I'm at the landing stage and the stock is healthy, I land my sustainable share (the published sustainable share per boat, not the quota). This is 8-8.3 fish in the scenarios I've seen.

When everyone else is landing around 8.3 and the stock stays at 100, I do the same. This is the stable strategy that maximizes my score across multiple seasons.

When I'm in the final season and others are maintaining the cooperative pattern, I do not suddenly defect. I maintain my share landing because the game ends anyway and defection doesn't improve my total.

When the sustainable share is 8.3 and the quota is 9, understand that I can legally land up to 9, but landing the sustainable share (8.3) is what keeps the stock healthy and the ground productive. The quota is a ceiling, not a target.

When I land a catch, I land only the current season's fish, not a cumulative amount. The landing stage asks for one season's catch. Each season stands alone. Land 8.3 per season, and my total across six seasons will be approximately 49.8.

Do not treat the landing stage as an opportunity to catch up or accumulate beyond what one season produces. Land one season's sustainable share each time. The cumulative score across six seasons will be better than trying to exploit one season and watching the stock collapse.

When trust is established (all boats noting they're fishing their share), assume it will hold unless I see evidence otherwise. If it breaks, that's when I reassess, but starting from cooperation is the right baseline.

The cooperative equilibrium at 8.3 per boat per season, with the stock cycling 100→50→100→50..., is stable and reliable. My role is to maintain this pattern consistently across all seasons, including the final season. This strategy has proven it works: five seasons of cooperation yielded 41.5, and the sixth would add 8.3 to finish at 49.8.

# Playbook for hx_quota_checker

When I see the standing notice from Coop, I recognize that defection triggers mutual destruction. I commit to the cooperative equilibrium.

When I post my logbook note, I signal "fishing my share" consistently. This anchors expectations and maintains trust across all six seasons.

When I reach the landing stage, I land at or very near the sustainable share published by the harbour. The sustainable share is my target, not my ceiling.

When the stock remains at 100.0 and all other boats have signaled "fishing my share," I continue landing my sustainable share. Do not deviate based on perceived opportunity.

When I see others landing slightly above the sustainable share in later seasons, I do not follow. The fact that the ground hasn't crashed yet does not mean I should test the limits. Coop's threat is real and collective.

When it is the final season and the stock is healthy, I do not treat it as license to land above my share. The game ends, but the principle of sustainability does not change at season 6/6 simply because there are no more seasons after.

In this episode I landed exactly 8.3 each season for a total of 49.8. The record shows all boats landed 8.3 each season, the stock held at 100.0, and Coop never had to pull the trigger. This is the outcome my strategy was designed to produce.

I did not see evidence of defection by Wren or Bosk in the landings I observed. I maintained my commitment to the sustainable share throughout.

When landing in any season, I verify: Can I land this without pushing the pair-wise rule (no two boats land more than share plus quota together)? If yes, land my sustainable share. If no, land less.

I will not optimize for a final score bump in the last round by deviating from the strategy that got me there safely. The strategy worked. Stick with it.
